claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy's dynamic behavior is controlled by a temperature- and strain-rate-induced transition between deformation twinning and discontinuous dynamic recrystallization.
Lower temperatures and higher strain rates produce twinning-dominated deformation in the Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy.
Removing Co lowers the effective stacking-fault energy of FeNiCrMn.
Lower effective stacking-fault energy promotes mechanical twinning.
Twinning at lower temperatures and higher strain rates raises strength while retaining ductility.
Higher temperatures and lower strain rates promote dynamic recrystallization.
Enhanced atomic mobility at elevated temperature is responsible for promoting dynamic recrystallization.
Discontinuous dynamic recrystallization refines the grain structure.
Dynamic recrystallization lowers the flow stress.
The initial Co-free alloy has an as-solidified, equiaxed, single-phase solid-solution microstructure similar to the Co-containing parent alloy.
Temperature and strain rate govern competition among dislocation slip, mechanical twinning, and grain-boundary-mediated dynamic recrystallization.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have higher flow stress at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have greater twin density at lower temperatures and higher strain rates.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show a marked decrease in flow stress.
At higher temperatures and lower strain rates, Co-free FeNiCrMn will undergo significant grain refinement through dynamic recrystallization.
The proposed mechanism applies approximately from 300 to 1273 K and from 0.1 to 0.001 s^-1.
